nodes.label: Linux Mint ISO distribution site compromise
nodes.summary: Attackers modified Linux Mint download infrastructure so some users received a backdoored ISO image instead of the legitimate distribution image.

nodes.label: CCleaner signed installer compromise
nodes.summary: A legitimate CCleaner release was modified and signed, distributing malware to downstream users through the normal software update and download path.

nodes.label: NotPetya distributed through M.E.Doc update channel
nodes.summary: The NotPetya destructive malware outbreak was seeded through a compromised Ukrainian accounting software update mechanism used by M.E.Doc customers.

nodes.label: eslint-scope npm package credential-stealing release
nodes.summary: An attacker used compromised npm maintainer credentials to publish malicious eslint-scope and eslint-config-eslint releases that attempted to steal npm tokens.

nodes.label: event-stream malicious dependency insertion
nodes.summary: A maintainer transfer enabled a malicious dependency to be added to the event-stream npm package dependency tree, targeting downstream cryptocurrency wallet software.

nodes.label: ASUS Live Update Operation ShadowHammer
nodes.summary: Attackers compromised the ASUS Live Update utility and distributed signed malicious updates to selected downstream systems.

nodes.label: Octopus Scanner malicious NetBeans project campaign
nodes.summary: Malicious code planted in open source NetBeans projects propagated through developer builds and attempted to infect additional projects.

nodes.label: SolarWinds Orion software build compromise
nodes.summary: Attackers compromised the SolarWinds Orion build process and inserted the SUNBURST backdoor into signed software updates delivered to customers.

nodes.label: Codecov Bash Uploader credential exfiltration
nodes.summary: The Codecov Bash Uploader was modified by an attacker, enabling environment variable and credential exfiltration from affected CI environments.

nodes.label: Dependency confusion proof-of-concept campaign
nodes.summary: Researchers demonstrated that public package registries could be abused to satisfy internal dependency names and execute code in downstream build environments.

nodes.label: Kaseya VSA ransomware supply-chain attack
nodes.summary: Attackers abused Kaseya VSA management software to distribute ransomware through managed service provider environments to downstream customers.

nodes.label: rc npm package malicious release
nodes.summary: The rc npm package had malicious versions published that required users to downgrade and inspect systems for suspicious activity.

nodes.label: PHP source repository backdoor attempt
nodes.summary: Attackers pushed malicious commits to the PHP source repository that would have introduced a backdoor if accepted into releases.

nodes.label: ua-parser-js npm package account compromise
nodes.summary: Malicious versions of ua-parser-js were published to npm after maintainer account compromise, delivering credential-stealing and cryptomining payloads.

nodes.label: colors and faker npm protestware releases
nodes.summary: The maintainer of colors and faker published intentionally disruptive releases that broke downstream consumers and demonstrated maintainer-driven supply-chain risk.

nodes.label: node-ipc peacenotwar protestware release
nodes.summary: The node-ipc npm package included protestware behavior that modified files for users in certain geographies, creating downstream integrity and availability risk.

nodes.label: ctx PyPI project account takeover
nodes.summary: The ctx project on PyPI was taken over and replaced with malicious code that collected environment variables from affected users.

nodes.label: PyTorch nightly dependency confusion compromise
nodes.summary: A malicious torchtriton package on PyPI was installed by some PyTorch nightly users because it shadowed an expected dependency name.

nodes.label: Ledger Connect Kit npm package compromise
nodes.summary: A compromised Ledger Connect Kit npm release injected malicious code into downstream web applications and targeted cryptocurrency wallet transactions.

nodes.label: 3CX desktop application software supply-chain compromise
nodes.summary: Attackers compromised 3CX desktop application builds, causing trojanized installers and updates to reach downstream customers.

nodes.label: LottieFiles lottie-player npm package compromise
nodes.summary: Compromised releases of the @lottiefiles/lottie-player npm package injected malicious wallet-draining code into downstream web applications.

nodes.label: Polyfill.io CDN script supply-chain compromise
nodes.summary: The Polyfill.io service began serving malicious JavaScript to downstream websites that embedded the third-party CDN script.

nodes.label: Ultralytics PyPI package compromise
nodes.summary: The ultralytics Python project suffered a supply-chain attack through compromised GitHub Actions workflows and PyPI publishing, resulting in malicious package releases.

nodes.label: XZ Utils backdoor attempt
nodes.summary: A backdoor was inserted into upstream XZ Utils release tarballs, affecting some downstream Linux distribution packaging before broad removal.

nodes.label: Go BoltDB typosquat module proxy backdoor
nodes.summary: Socket researchers disclosed a backdoored Go module typosquatting BoltDB that persisted through Go Module Proxy caching even after the source repository tag was changed.

nodes.label: Shai-Hulud npm self-propagating package compromise
nodes.summary: The Shai-Hulud campaign compromised npm packages with credential-harvesting malware that used stolen npm tokens to publish malicious versions of additional packages.

nodes.label: Shai-Hulud 2.0 npm supply-chain worm wave
nodes.summary: A second Shai-Hulud wave compromised hundreds of npm packages through install-time malware, GitHub token theft, and public repositories containing exfiltrated secrets.

nodes.label: tj-actions changed-files GitHub Action compromise
nodes.summary: The tj-actions/changed-files GitHub Action was compromised, exposing secrets from affected workflow runs through malicious action behavior.

nodes.label: Axios npm maintainer account compromise
nodes.summary: A compromised Axios maintainer account published malicious npm releases that added plain-crypto-js as an install-time dependency delivering a cross-platform remote access trojan.

nodes.label: Checkmarx Jenkins AST plugin supply-chain compromise
nodes.summary: Checkmarx reported that attackers used access traced to the Trivy supply-chain attack to publish malicious developer-tooling artifacts, including a modified Jenkins AST plugin.

nodes.label: LiteLLM PyPI package compromise through stolen CI/CD credentials
nodes.summary: Malicious LiteLLM versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 were published to PyPI with code not present in the upstream repository, exposing Python users and AI pipelines to credential theft.

nodes.label: Megalodon GitHub Actions repository workflow poisoning campaign
nodes.summary: The Megalodon campaign inserted malicious GitHub Actions workflows into thousands of public repositories to harvest CI/CD secrets and cloud credentials through automated commit activity.

nodes.label: Mini Shai-Hulud TanStack npm and PyPI supply-chain wave
nodes.summary: Mini Shai-Hulud compromised TanStack release automation and spread across npm and PyPI packages through trusted publishing, cache poisoning, and credential theft from CI/CD environments.

nodes.label: Nx Console VS Code extension compromise
nodes.summary: A malicious Nx Console 18.95.0 extension release was briefly distributed through VS Code and OpenVSX marketplaces, compromising developer systems and exposing credentials.

nodes.label: Aqua Trivy CI/CD supply-chain compromise
nodes.summary: Attackers compromised Trivy release and GitHub Action distribution paths, causing affected CI/CD environments to run credential-stealing code through trusted scanner workflows.

edges.summary: Hades is modeled as a suspected evolution of Miasma pending explicit code-overlap or researcher-attestation evidence.
Mini Shai-Hulud is modeled as the industrialized cross-ecosystem evolution of the Shai-Hulud worm pattern.
The second wave retained the Shai-Hulud worm playbook while increasing scale and propagation speed.
Checkmarx states that unauthorized GitHub access occurred due to the Trivy supply-chain attack, enabling malicious artifacts including the Jenkins plugin.
Snyk reports TeamPCP published the backdoored LiteLLM versions after obtaining maintainer PyPI credentials through the prior Trivy compromise.
Snyk reports TeamPCP published the backdoored LiteLLM versions after obtaining maintainer PyPI credentials through the prior Trivy compromise.

Mandiant documented the 3CX compromise as a cascade from a prior X_TRADER software supply-chain compromise; this edge records that public causal relationship without inferring additional downstream steps.
Public reporting places rxnt-authentication activity before the @ctrl/tinycolor wave and describes token reuse, but this edge is temporal precedence rather than asserted package-to-package causation.
The npm registry metadata records adjacent malicious @ctrl/tinycolor releases on the same date; this edge preserves ordered wave structure without asserting causation.
The same malicious plain-crypto-js dependency was introduced into both compromised Axios release lines.
The Axios postmortem and Google analysis describe malicious Axios releases depending on plain-crypto-js 4.2.1 as the install-time payload carrier.
IronWorm is a suspected sibling clone over the released base rather than a confirmed descendant.
Miasma is treated as a suspected fork from the released framework unless stronger code-overlap or researcher-attestation evidence lands.
